message.reasoning:
We need to choose a liquidation action to raise cash to pay owed amount 310, we have cash 50, shortfall 260? Actually owed 310, cash 50, shortfall 260. Wait shortfall listed 290? Owed 310, cash 50 => shortfall 260. But they list shortfall 290 maybe includes other fees? Anyway need to raise at least owed amount.

We have properties: Pennsylvania Railroad (unmortgaged), B&O Railroad, Kentucky Avenue with 3 houses, Indiana Avenue 3 houses, Illinois Avenue 3 houses. Also we have mortgageable space keys list includes WATER_WORKS (we don't own), READING_RAILROAD (not owned), PENNSYLVANIA_RAILROAD (owned), B_O_RAILROAD (owned). So we can mortgage either railroad. Mortgage value is half purchase price. Standard Monopoly: Railroads cost $200 each, mortgage value $100. So mortgaging one gives $100 cash.

We also can sell houses/hotels from listed sellable building space keys. Those include our three with 3 houses each: Kentucky, Indiana, Illinois. Also other spaces we don't own. Selling houses: each house sells for half purchase price. Purchase price: Kentucky Avenue (orange) cost $220, houses cost $50 each? Actually houses on orange cost $50. So each house sells for $25. We have 3 houses each on three properties = 9 houses total. Selling all 9 houses yields 9 * $25 = $225. But we must sell evenly across monopoly: must sell houses evenly across properties in a color group. We have monopoly of orange (Kentucky, Indiana, Illinois) with 3 houses each. To sell houses, we must sell from any property but keep even distribution. So we could sell 1 house from each property (3 houses total) to get $75, leaving 2 houses each. Could sell 2 houses from each (6 houses) for $150, leaving 1 house each. Could sell all 3 houses from each (9 houses) for $225, leaving 0 houses (monopoly with no houses). That's allowed as long as we sell evenly. So we could raise $225.

We need at least 260? Actually shortfall 290 per scenario. Let's assume need 310 total, we have 50, need 260. So selling all houses gives 225, still short 35. Then we could mortgage a railroad for $100, raising total 325, enough. But we could also mortgage first then sell fewer houses. Need to choose exactly one liquidation action now. The engine will apply it, then ask again if still cannot pay. So we should pick the most efficient action that raises enough cash, maybe mortgage one railroad (100) and then later sell houses if still short. But we can only do one action now. If we mortgage one railroad, we get $100, cash becomes 150, still short 160. Then we will need another liquidation later. Could also sell houses now: selling all houses gives $225, cash becomes 275, still short 35, then need another action (mortgage). Might be better to mortgage first because we might want to keep houses for rent later? But houses generate rent; selling them reduces future income. However we are low on cash and need to pay rent to Gamma. If we cannot pay, we might go bankrupt. So we need to raise enough cash soon. Perhaps best to mortgage a railroad (100) and also sell houses? But only one action allowed. Could we sell houses and also mortgage in same action? No.

We could sell houses partially to raise enough cash without mortgaging. If we sell 6 houses (2 from each) we get $150, cash becomes 200, still short 110. Not enough. Sell all 9 houses gives $225, cash 275, still short 35. So still need mortgage. So either way need at least two actions. But we can choose the action that yields the most cash now: selling all houses yields 225, mortgage yields 100. So better to sell houses now, then next step mortgage. So choose sell_houses_or_hotel with sell_plan for each of the three orange properties, kind HOUSE, count 3 each? Actually we need to sell all houses: each property has 3 houses, we sell 3 houses from each. That will remove all houses. So sell_plan list of three entries.

Make public_message maybe "Selling houses to raise cash." Private thought: reasoning.
